facts.statement: The species Agaleus dorsetensis is known only from isolated teeth.
facts.quote: This species is currently only known from isolated teeth.

facts.statement: Agaleus is an extinct stem-galeomorph shark that lived during the Early Jurassic Epoch.
facts.quote: Agaleus is an extinct genus of stem-galeomorph shark from the Early Jurassic Epoch.

facts.statement: While some authorities once placed Agaleus as a basal member of the order Orectolobiformes, later research classified it as a stem-galeomorph outside that crown group.
facts.quote: Some authorities have placed this species as a basal member of the order Orectolobiformes, but subsequent researchers have found it to be a stem-galeomorph just outside the crown group of Orectolobiformes.

facts.statement: Fossils of Agaleus have been found in the Hettangian-Sinemurian of Lyme Regis, England, and the Pliensbachian-aged Hasle Formation of Denmark and Grimmen clay pit in north-eastern Germany.
facts.quote: It is known from the Hettangian-Sinemurian of Lyme Regis, England and the Pliensbachian-aged Hasle Formation of Denmark and Grimmen clay pit of north-eastern Germany.

facts.statement: Agaleus fossils have also been discovered in Northern Ireland, France, Belgium, and Sweden.
facts.quote: Other places which have produced this species include Northern Ireland, France, Belgium, and Sweden.

facts.statement: Agaleus lived from the Sinemurian to the Toarcian stages, between 199.5 and 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Toarcian (199.5 to 174.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Agaleus is the oldest known unambiguous crown group shark.
rejected.quote: It is the oldest known unambiguous crown group shark.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is the oldest known unambiguous crown group shark'
